Why Cairn

Make space.
Keep your place.

A full disk should not turn into another project. Cairn is being built to make the next storage decision easier to understand.

For people who build

The work behind the files.

A developer’s Mac holds more than code. Dependencies, simulators, caches and generated output share space with repositories, credentials and the conversations that help a project move forward.

Cairn starts with that distinction. It brings the storage picture, individual review and the outcome into one native macOS workflow.

The aim is a useful decision: understand what is there, know the consequence of an action, and keep a record you can inspect afterwards.

A mark along the way

Why “Cairn”?

A cairn is a stack of stones that marks a path. The name stands for a clearer next step when your Mac is full.

The four rounded blue stones are Cairn’s mark. They belong with the quiet graphite surfaces and clear blue accents of the app and this site.

The approach

Care should be visible.

Explain the path

Show which item is involved, what was measured and what an action will do.

Keep evidence separate

A candidate estimate, a recorded action and an observed increase in free space are different facts.

Say what is uncertain

Incomplete scans and unfinished release validation should be visible, not hidden behind a confident number.

A product in development

There is no public download or open checkout yet. This site describes current work and its limits. App previews use labelled sample data.

For the work ahead

Find your next step.

Understand the workflow before deciding what goes.
